subject: Post-call: Crestview inference topology & SLO alignment
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@crestview.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:12:08 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Crestview inference topology & SLO alignment

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while items are fresh: 

Key pain points you described:
- High variance in tail latency for document indexing (p95 spikes to 1.2s during ingestion bursts).
- Cost unpredictability from per-request autoscaling on cloud GPUs; desire to control unit economics for peak traffic.
- Need for on-premise processing for PHI-regulated datasets in one of your clinics.

Goals you want to hit in the next 90 days:
1) Stable p95 latency <= 400ms for search reranks under typical load (50 qps avg, 200 qps burst).
2) Predictable monthly inference cost within +/- 15% vs current baseline.
3) Private deployment option for PHI workflows with customer-managed VPC and KMS.

Technical notes / model requirements you mentioned:
- Primary model: open Llama-2 70B (quantized candidate), occasional 2k context length for long documents.
- Typical request size: 150-600 tokens; batchable during offline indexing; low-latency path for interactive rerank.

Preliminary topology we discussed (see attached topology sketch to follow):
- Hosted Redwood API for low-friction evaluation and canary.
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved G4dn-like instances) for predictable throughput on rerank workloads.
- Private VPC deployment for PHI ingestion pipeline (same runtime, customer-managed network).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Daniel: send sample latency traces and 7-day traffic histogram (you mentioned infra can export) — ETA 48h.
- Aditya: draft sizing and batching strategy for 50/200 qps profiles — ETA 72h.
- Vivek: list of security/compliance prerequisites for Private deployment (KMS, audit retention) — ETA EOW.
- Lauren: consolidate notes and share mutual action plan + a first-pass cost estimate — ETA 48h.

Attachments: I referenced a short template for the mutual action plan (will attach a one-pager "redwood_proposal_draft_v1.pdf") and suggested you export a sample CSV of request latencies (crestview_latency_sample.csv).

If I missed anything important, please flag. I'll follow up once I have Aditya's sizing notes and a draft M.A.P.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0197

Subject: Re: Post-call: Crestview inference topology & SLO alignment

Thanks Lauren — solid recap. Attaching the latency export from our staging cluster (crestview_latency_sample.csv). Couple clarifications: 

1) The p95 spikes to ~1.2s appear tied to two patterns: long-tail model context switches (when some requests request full-document concat) and simultaneous batch flushes during index jobs.
2) For PHI, our legal team prefers bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and retention windows of 90 days.
3) We can start with LLaMA-2-70B quant at 4-bit; if results are poor we may try a distilled 13B fallback for higher throughput.

Also, would like a rough runbook of how Redwood will handle regional failover — specifically: if our primary US region has capacity issues, how quickly can requests fail-over to a warmed Dedicated pool in another region (we understand data residency constraints but curious about recommended patterns).

Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of ML Platforms, Crestview Analytics
daniel.park@crestview.ai | +1 (212) 555-0124

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 8:03 PM Daniel Park <daniel.park@crestview.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Lauren — solid recap. Attaching the latency export from our staging cluster (crestview_latency_sample.csv).
> 
> Also, would like a rough runbook of how Redwood will handle regional failover...

Thanks for the dataset, Daniel — reviewed the CSV quickly. My read / recommendations: 

- Batching profile: 60% of requests are low-latency interactive (<200 tokens) and are best served on a continuous-batching low-latency pool (max batch-size 8, max-wait 8ms). The other 40% are larger indexing jobs (400-1,800 tokens) that we should route to a dedicated throughput pool (larger batch-size 32+, asynchronous prioritization).
- Model strategy: start with quantized Llama-2-70B on dedicated throughput nodes with KV cache pinned; provide a 13B distilled variant on low-latency nodes to ensure p95 coverage during bursts. Automatic fallback rule: if p95 > 600ms on low-latency pool, route interactive requests to 13B pool until warm.
- Topology sketch: 1) Hosted evaluation zone (us-west) for quick trials (no PHI). 2) Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) colocated in us-east for steady rerank traffic. 3) Private VPC cluster in customer account for PHI ingestion with S3 endpoint + BYOK.
- Failover note: warm standby Dedicated capacity in another region is feasible; typical warm-up is 2-8 minutes depending on model and KV cache size. For strict <1min failover you need pre-warmed standby instances and cross-region cache replication which has cost trade-offs. Recommend a canary-simulated failover test during POC.

I'll put these into a short diagram and sizing table and share the draft PDF (redwood_proposal_draft_v1.pdf).

- Aditya

Attachment stub: redwood_proposal_draft_v1.pdf (proposal draft, 1 page)

Daniel — thanks for the trace and the clarifications. Next steps and tentative calendar: 

1) Aditya to share sizing + MAP draft (attached) — ETA 24h.
2) Vivek to share Private deployment security checklist (KMS BYOK, audit log retention, network peering notes) — ETA EOW.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Crestview infra + ML platforms next Wed 06/02 at 10:00am ET (I sent a calendar invite). Goal: review sample traffic, confirm p95 target, agree on failover pattern and initial reserved capacity.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Week 0: POC kickoff — sample data ingestion to hosted Redwood evaluation instance (no PHI).
- Week 1-2: Dedicated pool sizing + 2-week smoke tests with simulated bursts.
- Week 3: Private VPC deployment validation with BYOK and audit hooks (in a staging environment).
- Week 4+: Pilot to production roll (canary + A/B traffic shift).

Risks we flagged: model quality at quantized 70B, cache warming time for long-context requests, and cross-region failover latency. We'll include mitigation options in the MAP PDF.

If that aligns, we'll proceed and I’ll loop in Solutions Engineering for the deep-dive prep.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
